subject: Console per-route breakout and SLA guardrails for MapleHealth
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-25T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Notes from MapleHealth — per-route visibility + SLA guardrails

Quick summary from this morning's call with Sara (MapleHealth): they need a way in the Console to understand per-route economics (cost + latency) at a glance and a set of automated guardrails that flag SLA drift. They framed this as a product request but also an operational requirement: if their SLA exposure spikes we should surface it and provide a one-click mitigation (roll back to smaller model / route-level fallback).

Asks they called out explicitly: 
- Console popover on each route showing: 7/30/90d cost, 95p latency, and token breakdown (prompt vs completion).
- Exportable CSV (per-route rows) with timestamped snapshots.
- SLA drift alerts: when 95p latency or per-1k-token cost increases by >25% vs 30d baseline.
- Short-term workaround: a manual snapshot export they can consume until we ship the UI.

Constraints / notes for scope: 
- MapleHealth expects 90-day retention for these snapshots and CSV export.
- They want the SLA guardrails to be region-aware (US-only for now).
- They may want to pin a fallback policy (e.g., fall back from redwood-large -> redwood-medium) when alerts fire.

Could each of you reply with: 
1) backend feasibility and estimated effort (Marcus) 
2) minimal telemetry/aggregation design we need (Jasmine) 
3) rollout & guardrail policy design + owner suggestions (Irene)

I'm cc'ing the mockups + the requirements spreadsheet (attached). Hoping to give MapleHealth a tentative plan by Monday.

Thanks — Soojin

Attachments: maple_health_requirements.xlsx, console-popover-mockup.png
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-26T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notes from MapleHealth — per-route visibility + SLA guardrails

Thanks Soojin — good brief. Quick technical readout and a small proposal attached.

Feasibility: doable with current telemetry and the path-econ pipeline but there are a few gotchas: 
- Sampling: we currently store full per-token cost traces for 3 days, aggregated histograms for 30 days, and sparse summaries for 90 days. To meet MapleHealth's CSV requirements we'll need an hourly rollup job that writes snapshots to longer-term storage (S3) and a small query layer to produce per-route CSVs on demand.
- Latency percentiles: computing 95p at fine granularity across many tenants is expensive; I recommend precomputing 50/95/99 per-route per-hour windows and materializing daily and weekly aggregates.
- Fallback automation: the runtime can support model-variant fallback, but we need a safe coupling between alerting rules and a routing policy engine. That's extra dev (+ QA).

Estimated effort: 
- Minimal prototype (backend rollup + one CSV export endpoint): 2.5 dev-weeks (1 backend SWE + 0.5 infra).
- Full feature (materialized aggregates, console popover, alert-to-fallback pipeline): ~6 dev-weeks across backend/frontend/infra.

I've attached a short per-route-sampling-proposal.pdf that sketches the rollup job and retention model. Questions: do we need per-customer encryption-at-rest for these snapshots (MapleHealth is in healthcare — likely yes).

Attachments: per-route-sampling-proposal.pdf

On 2028-04-25, Soojin Lee wrote:
> Quick summary from this morning's call with Sara (MapleHealth): they need a way in the Console to understand per-route economics (cost + latency) at a glance and a set of automated guardrails that flag SLA drift.

— Marcus
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-27T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notes from MapleHealth — per-route visibility + SLA guardrails

Couple of product/ops points to add: 
1) Guardrail semantics: we should define two modes — alert-only (default) and automated mitigation (opt-in). For health customers like MapleHealth we can offer automated mitigation behind an explicit contract clause.
2) Ownership: frontend (console) should own the popover UX and export button; backend owns the rollup pipelines and CSV endpoint. Ops should own the alerting rules and the playbook.
3) Rollout: start with a 1-customer beta (MapleHealth), then open to a small early-access group. Use a feature flag for the frontend and an infra flag for backend behavior.

I've created a short ticket to capture the guardrail playbook and first-pass runbook: JIRA-INF-8421. Marcus: can you add the estimated infra cost (S3 + query infra) to that ticket? Jasmine: please add the minimal telemetry tags we need there as well.

On 2028-04-26, Marcus Lin wrote:
> Feasibility: doable with current telemetry and the path-econ pipeline but there are a few gotchas...

— Irene
From: Sara Vasquez <sara.vasquez@maplehealth.org>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-28T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notes from MapleHealth — per-route visibility + SLA guardrails

Thanks, Soojin — appreciate the quick follow-up. A few clarifications from our side that will affect sampling and CSV columns: 
- Metrics: 95th percentile latency (ms), mean latency, total tokens, cost per 1k tokens (USD). We typically look at rolling windows (daily / weekly / 30d) but want the ability to slice by region (US-EAST, US-WEST).
- Timezone: show data in UTC and include an explicit timestamp column in the CSV.
- Retention: 90-day retention is required; we may request extended export history during audits.
- Security: all exports must be accessible only to MapleHealth org admins; we will require SSO-based downloads (ok to use a presigned S3 link behind SSO).

We can join a technical alignment call to walk through sample CSV columns — I'm attaching a small spreadsheet that lists the columns we expect.

Thanks — Sara

Attachments: maple_health_requirements.xlsx
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Sara Vasquez <sara.vasquez@maplehealth.org>
Date: 2028-04-30T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notes from MapleHealth — per-route visibility + SLA guardrails

Thanks everyone — good alignment. Quick agreed next steps and owners: 
- Marcus: prototype backend rollup + CSV endpoint. Target: prototype by 2028-05-14. Add infra cost estimate to JIRA-INF-8421.
- Jasmine: add telemetry tag list + hourly materialization plan to the ticket by 2028-05-07.
- Irene: write guardrail runbook draft and author the feature flag policy for the beta by 2028-05-10.
- Soojin: schedule a 45-min alignment call with MapleHealth for 2028-05-03; invite includes product + security.

Sara: I'll send the calendar invite now for 2028-05-03 10:00am PT. If that doesn't work feel free to propose alternatives.

I'll keep the mockups and the requirements spreadsheet on the ticket. Flag me if anyone needs help with the SSO/export constraints — security will need to weigh in before we give presigned links.

Thanks — Soojin
